hypothesis: The implemented rail ledger, state word, clock-token status and native adapter meet the instruction, line, lock and storage budgets of the power-authority design, measured against the merge base.
prediction: Rail status for a one-rail token at most 60 instructions and 3 lines; clock token status at most 50 instructions with no scan; acquire, poll and release at most 450 instructions with no bus access; authority check per PMIC transaction one acquire load of at most 6 instructions; ledger at most 1,632 B; counter-clock lock acquisitions at most 2 per snapshot and per selector write; setup reads 3 plus 3 after each STOP (21 and 27); 7 DSB SY per read transaction and 5 per write; 0 polls ticks with the service task.

conclusion: Every implemented budget holds (rail status, clock status, acquire-poll-release, authority check, ledger size, counter-clock lock count); three rows stay outside their targets for the stated reasons (setup reads, DSB SY count, polls per snapshot). No measured performance metric is worse than the base. The package objects shrink by 256 B. Board evidence (PMU cycles on A55 and A76, S_TWI0 bus timing and spin lengths, a lighter barrier placement) is still required.
narrative:
Host-modeled figures only (instruction emulation or host model); none comes from the board. Merge base / measured (design target):
- Rail status, one-rail token, small / full: 222 / 888 instructions, 34 / 256 lines -> 37 / 37, 3 / 3 lines (<= 60, <= 3 lines).
- Clock token status, 42 / 126 leases: 235 / 592 instructions -> 45 / 45 (<= 50, no scan). Rail and clock status cost the same with 16 and with 31 holders, so neither scans.
- Acquire, poll and release: 1,643 / 3,565 -> 335 / 335, no bus access (<= 450).
- Borrow; end borrow, small / full: 823 / 1,531; 271 / 923 -> 153 / 153; 86 / 86.
- Authority check per PMIC transaction: 498 / 1,507 instructions, 68 / 353 lines -> 6 / 6, 1 line (one acquire load, <= 6 instructions).
- Ledger 20,096 B -> 1,600 B (<= 1,632 B). Clock registry 6,208 B -> 6,208 B.
- Time reads per snapshot; per selector write: 590; 732 -> 469; 599.
- Counter-clock lock acquisitions per snapshot; selector write: 590; 732 (one per time read) -> 0; 0 (<= 2; <= 2).
- Mutex-holder queries: 250; 309 -> 1; 1 at bus entry (1 per request). In the merge-base adapter every register access queried the kernel mutex holder, which enters a kernel critical section in this FreeRTOS SMP kernel, so the query count equalled its register accesses.
- Register accesses: 250; 309 -> 211; 270.
- Setup reads per snapshot; per selector write: 64; 70 -> 25; 31 (target 3 plus 3 after each STOP: 21; 27). Not met: admission rereads the S_TWI0 clock route and divisor (four or five reads) because checks/a733-clock-reference-pmic.c requires drift detection there.
- DSB SY per snapshot; selector write: 500; 618 (two per register access) -> 422; 540 (target 7 per read transaction, 5 per write). Not met: the adapter keeps DSB SY before and after each register access until a board run completes snapshots and selector writes with identical results under both placements; docs/shared-helpers.md requires that qualification for a weaker barrier.
- Polls per snapshot; per selector write (model): 44; 56 -> 44; 56 (target 0 ticks with the service task). Longest poll; BUSY per snapshot (model): 58 us; 591 us -> 17 us; 470 us. Not met in this package: the service task needs a second task-notification index and a scheduled-core constant from the primary agent (see power-domains records).
- Image .text, board / HDMI / storage maintenance: 496,940 / 120,768 / 179,852 B -> 494,828 / 118,712 / 177,804 B. Image .bss (llvm-size -A): 1,201,856 / 382,032 / 437,952 B -> 1,183,424 / 363,600 / 419,520 B; each image shrinks by 18,432 B (ledger reduction less alignment). Total image .bss, board / HDMI / storage maintenance, from the implementation note: 5,502,352 / 465,376 / 541,776 B -> 5,481,872 / 446,944 / 523,344 B.
- Package object code, five power and clock objects: 25,369 B -> 25,113 B. Per object (base -> measured): a733_pmic.c 10,948 -> 12,176 B; a733_pmic_native.c 1,701 -> 1,965 B; a733_rail_leases.c 5,832 -> 4,080 B; a733_clock_leases.c 3,456 -> 3,468 B; a733_pmic_consumer.c 3,432 -> 3,424 B.
- Provider growth of 1,228 B: the per-phase transfer function grows 716 B and the register helpers 100 B each (inlined state-word check and fault-bit write replacing the per-phase borrow and clock-registry queries), the new route function adds 576 B, the startup-only baseline check shrinks 420 B. The native adapter grows 264 B (raw counter read and holding flag). The ledger shrinks 1,752 B, so package objects shrink 256 B and each image .text about 2 KiB.
- Native-adapter costs per request follow from the adapter source and the register-access counts: in the base adapter every time read calls a733_counter_clock_now, every register access queries the I2C mutex holder, and every register access carries a DSB SY before and after it; in the measured adapter the time read is ISB; MRS CNTPCT_EL0 with no lock, the holder is queried once at bus entry, and the barriers are unchanged.

- Clock token status: 243 / 600 instructions -> <= 50, no scan.
- Acquire, poll and release: 4,026 / 7,773 instructions -> <= 450, no bus access.
- Authority check per PMIC transaction: 818 / 2,179 instructions -> 1 acquire load, <= 6 instructions.
- Provider object acquisitions per request: one per phase poll -> 2, none during the transfer.
- Counter-clock lock acquisitions per snapshot; write; PCK600 transition; CPU settle: one per poll -> 2; 2; 1; 1, independent of spin length.
- DSB SY per PMIC transaction -> 7 per read, 5 per write. Setup reads per request: about 50 -> 3, plus 3 after each STOP.
- Snapshot, submit to requester wake: up to one tick per step -> 4 transactions, <= 0.45 ms busy, 0 ticks. Selector write: 6 transactions, <= 0.65 ms busy, 0 ticks.
- Supply verification: six drivers, each on use -> 16 transactions, about 1.8 ms, once per boot (the owner as built verifies DCDC2 and DCDC4 with 12 transactions).
- Row request, first or later: GPU 27 polls and one supply read -> 0 PMIC requests, 1 acquire load.
- Barriers per row request; per transition: about 10 DSB SY; 2 per status poll -> 0; 1 after the command, plus the NPU's 1 after its CCU writes.

- Service task idle wakes per second: one per loop iteration -> 0. BUSY results after a publication wake, single core -> 0.
- 200 us USB0 burst on core 0 during a PMIC snapshot and write, single core and SMP with the snapshot on core 2: every phase deadline holds; <= 2 counter-clock acquisitions by the service task per request.
- Ledger storage 20,096 B -> <= 1,632 B (static assertion).

conclusion: Targets recorded as designed; the measured outcome of the implemented subset is in record power-authority-host-measurements, and the unimplemented parts are open work in the design document.
narrative:
Design inputs for the superseded service-task proposal: a733_pmic_service would replace the PMIC loops of the board and OS images and of camera, gpu-display, gpu-render, gpu-finite, hdmi, i2s, mimus, npu-convolution, npu-returning, thermal-returning, usb-returning and storage-update, at priority 3 below the USB0, audio, headset and thermal tasks, with affinity A733_PMIC_SERVICE_CORES (A55 cores 2-5 where the scheduler starts them, core 0 in single-core images; checks/pmic-* fails if the mask is not a subset of the image's scheduled cores). Requesters would wait with ulTaskNotifyTakeIndexed on A733_NOTIFY_INDEX_POWER (index 1 of configTASK_NOTIFICATION_ARRAY_ENTRIES 2), timeout the ticks left before the deadline; a BUSY retried after a one-tick wait; publication would store DONE or EXPIRED, copy and clear the task handle, leave the object and only then notify, unless the provider fault bit was set; checks/pmic-* would fail if vTaskDelete appeared in the tree. A snapshot is four single-register transactions (page, enable, selector, page); a write adds a selector write and a readback. Chip identity, the S_TWI0 gate and reset word and the divisor are checked once at verify; the three bus-idle registers are read at activation and after every STOP. Only the provider names the S_TWI0 interrupt, GIC-600 INTID 235 (twi@7083000, SPI 203 in board-kernel/sun60iw2p1.dtsi). The service task that exists is described in power-domains.md; requesters still poll a733_pmic_result once per tick and no requester notifications exist.

Packet-engine threshold: the pinned board device tree sets twi_drv_used = <1> on s_twi0, so the vendor driver uses the TWI packet engine (TWI_DRV_CTRL, TWI_DRV_INT_CTRL, a FIFO and DMA request 47), which raises one completion per transaction on INTID 235, about 6 per write, with no per-byte CPU work. A spun write costs about 0.65 ms of A55 time plus 0.3 ms of settle spin on a CPU rail; at 10 CPU voltage changes per second that is about 1% of one core. The design replaces the byte spin by the packet engine when the measured voltage-change rate exceeds 10 per second or the engine is qualified on the board.

Model cases the design listed: checks/rail-leases.c (acquire, poll and release in production order; READY on first poll for all fifteen rails; full table returns BUSY); checks/a733-pmic.c (submit before READY returns BUSY; a fault raised on another core during startup stays latched after READY; a registry fault during a write faults the provider before the selector-write byte; a fault during a spin stops all later TWI access); checks/a733-pmic-polls.c (priority-5 requester woken by publication reaps within the deadline with no BUSY; a higher-priority requester preempting the service task during activation blocks one tick; no spin makes a counter-clock call; the single-core and SMP USB0 burst rows); checks/power-domains-pck.c (boot verification issues 16 transactions in the design, 12 as built, and no row request issues a PMIC read; a mismatched DCDC4 refuses the GPU row; incoherent domains 4 and 1 are refused before any NPU or framebuffer reset or clock write; domain-4 write order including the DSB SY after the CCU writes matches checks/npu-platform.c; a DisplayPort request that retains domain 10 sets its fault bit; an open GPU gate refuses power-off; a second requester observes FAILED within the bound); checks/cpu-clock-model.c (the target never falls below the baseline).

hypothesis: Board evidence that would confirm the power-authority design.
prediction:
- The S_TWI0 SCL rate for divisor 0x28; the packet engine's register behavior, and whether it reads 0x10 and 0x11 in one transaction.
- DCDC3 and DCDC5 readbacks after a raise and a lowering, with request-to-readback times and the longest spins.
- Unchanged DCDC2-5 selectors and PMIC page 0 after PSCI CPU_ON, and a bus capture showing no other S_TWI0 master. (The scheme relies on no agent writing DCDC2 and DCDC4 after boot; the OS issues no PSCI CPU_OFF or suspend call and checks/pmic-* fails if such a function identifier appears.)
- PCK600 time to ON for domains 1, 4, 5 and 10 and to OFF for domain 5.
- USB0 and audio latency with PMIC requests running, in an SMP and a single-core image.
- PMU cycles for rail and clock status on an A55 and an A76.
- A schematic source for the DE_SYS, G2D and deinterlace supply.
conclusion: Not yet run; each item is open work.

hypothesis: Where the implementation differs from the original power-authority design, and why.
conclusion: Differences are intentional and each has a stated reason.
narrative: Differences recorded when the package was measured: a733_pmic_live takes no lock (it compares the immutable lifetime and makes one acquire load of the state word, so it never returns BUSY). Request admission rereads the clock route and divisor (four or five reads) because checks/a733-clock-reference-pmic.c requires drift detection there. Exclusive tokens remain accepted on all fifteen outputs as pure exclusion; checks/a733-radio-platform.c expects BUSY, not INVALID, for an exclusive DCDC8 request; DC1SW1 is accepted as a DCDC1 alias with DC1SW2. The CPU floor lives in the ledger (a733_rail_floor) because include/a733_cpu_clock.h was outside the package. The native adapter's time read returns the raw counter in microseconds (ISB; MRS CNTPCT_EL0 divided by the ticks per microsecond) instead of calling the counter clock once per poll and comparing raw ticks; it gives the same microseconds with no lock, so the provider and struct a733_pmic_ops stay unchanged (checks outside the package build that structure with positional initializers, which a new field would break under -Wmissing-field-initializers). The provider's monotonic check faults on a counter that runs backwards, the time read refuses after a fault latched in the shared counter clock, and the provider has no spin for an iteration cap to bound; checks/pmic-tree.py fails if the time read calls the counter clock. The native adapter checks mutex ownership once per bus entry because a FreeRTOS mutex changes holder only when its holder gives it and only the adapter's leave gives it on the provider task. The adapter keeps DSB SY before and after each register access. The DE_SYS provider a733_de_sys_power.c is deleted; the power-domain owner has no domain-9 or domain-10 entry. The design's CLDO2 and CLDO5 verified bits and domain-10 fault bit are not implemented; the NPU startup now uses its domain-4 row.
